Pad operations before ignition.requires: vehicle stationary, crew and ground systems connected
Pad operations before ignition.provides: full physical access, no flight dynamics, unlimited time to decide

First-stage ascent.requires: engines running, vehicle within the atmosphere
First-stage ascent.provides: maximum aerodynamic load, range safety coverage, seconds of decision time

Stage separation.requires: first stage burnout, pyrotechnic or pneumatic release
Stage separation.provides: a single irreversible event lasting under a second, high structural transient

Upper-stage burn.provides: no aerodynamic load, beyond most ground radar, minutes of burn

Orbital insertion.provides: final trim only, no gross thrust available, no range safety coverage

Propulsion.provides: loss of thrust, no redundant channel, immediate trajectory effect

Guidance and navigation.provides: wrong trajectory with engines healthy, usually a redundant channel available

Structural airframe.provides: irreversible breakup, no redundancy, no recovery path

Ground support equipment.provides: faults only while connected, fully recoverable, no flight consequence

Payload fairing.requires: atmospheric flight or a separation event
Payload fairing.provides: payload exposure or retained mass, no effect on propulsion or guidance

Pad camera and acoustics.requires: the vehicle within sight and earshot of the pad
Pad camera and acoustics.provides: immediate observation on the ground only

Onboard telemetry downlink.requires: powered avionics and a link to a ground station
Onboard telemetry downlink.provides: subsystem-level data throughout flight, lost if the vehicle is destroyed

Ground tracking radar.provides: position and velocity only, no subsystem detail, lost beyond the horizon

Post-flight debris recovery.provides: physical evidence weeks later, nothing in real time

Hold and safe the vehicle.requires: the vehicle not yet committed to flight

Abort and range destruct.requires: range safety coverage and a vehicle inside it
Abort and range destruct.provides: controlled destruction, total loss of vehicle and payload

Switch to redundant channel.requires: a redundant unit to exist for that subsystem

Accept degraded orbit.requires: the payload already near a usable orbit

_v1_notes.FLIGHT PHASE|FAILED SUBSYSTEM: ground support equipment can only fail while physically connected, so it is Y on the pad and N everywhere after. Structural failure on the pad is N: there is no mechanical flight load before ignition. Fairing failure is N on the pad (not yet loaded) and N at insertion (already jettisoned). Fairing at upper-stage burn is Y only if not yet separated - here N, since separation precedes upper-stage burn on most vehicles.
_v1_notes.FLIGHT PHASE|DETECTION: pad cameras see only the pad, so N for everything after first-stage ascent. Radar is N on the pad (stationary, nothing to track), N at upper-stage burn and insertion (beyond the horizon). Debris recovery is N on the pad because nothing has flown.
_v1_notes.FLIGHT PHASE|MITIGATION: hold and safe requires a vehicle not yet committed, so Y only on the pad. Range destruct requires range safety coverage, which exists during ascent and separation but not on the pad (never destruct a fuelled vehicle on the pad) nor at orbital altitude. Degraded orbit is meaningful only once near orbit.
_v1_notes.FAILED SUBSYSTEM|DETECTION: guidance failure is invisible to pad cameras, radar (which sees position, not why) and debris. Ground support faults never leave the pad, so telemetry, radar and debris are all N. Fairing failure is invisible to radar.
_v1_notes.FAILED SUBSYSTEM|MITIGATION: propulsion has no redundant channel, so N. Structural failure admits neither redundancy nor a degraded orbit - the vehicle is gone. Ground support faults never warrant destruct and never produce a degraded orbit. Fairing failure has no redundant channel.
_v1_notes.DETECTION|MITIGATION: debris recovery is post-hoc and supports no mitigation at all. Pad cameras cannot support a degraded-orbit decision. Radar gives position only, insufficient to decide a redundancy switch, and cannot support hold-and-safe since the vehicle has flown.
